title: Can a Network of Miniature Sponge Cities Help Central Asia Curb Climate Change?
author: Walt Ohnesorge
text:
Condos in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan, often use scarce potable water to support non-native plants such as roses.
Credit: Walt Ohnesorge
Can gardens act as a network of miniature sponge cities to have a positive impact on climate change in Central Asia? A preponderance of aesthetic decisions and other barriers hold back the adaptation of Central Asia’s cities, but individuals and local authorities can make a difference.Kyrgyzstan, and Central Asia more broadly, are experiencing stress on available groundwater reserves. As Dr. Eric Rudenshiold noted in an article for the Caspian Policy Center last year, “Driven by regional temperature increases, the region’s glaciers are melting at a rate four times faster than the global average and far faster than anticipated.”[...]
